summary: Adolf Kiessling studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1856–1858) and taught Wilhelm Schulze. He held posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1872), the University of Greifswald (~1872–1877), and the University of Göttingen (~1889–1893).

A scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology, Kirchhoff studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1846) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He held posts at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and Frederick William University Berlin (~1865–1908).
Linguist Adolf Noreen studied at Uppsala University (~1871–1877) and under August Leskien (~1879). He spent his career as a faculty member at Uppsala University (~1887–1919).

Active in history and archaeology, Adolf Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich (~1847–1849), where he became a Privatdozent in 1850. In 1854, he was employed for exploration by the East India Company.

Linguist Adolf Tobler studied at the University of Zurich (~1853–1854) and the University of Bonn (~1854–1857) under Friedrich Christian Diez and Nikolaus Delius. He taught Alfons Hilka and held a long-term post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1867–1910).

Adolfo Esteller y Melià was an Indologist and linguist who earned doctorates at the Pontifical Gregorian University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1937–1964) and directed the Heras Institute (1956–1963).

Linguist Adolphe Pictet studied at the universities of Geneva, Paris, Berlin (under G. W. F. Hegel), Edinburgh, and London. He taught Ferdinand de Saussure and served as Privatdozent at the University of Geneva from 1840 to 1844.

Active in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, Adolphe Regnier studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at Lycée Saint-Louis, Lycée Charlemagne, Collège de France, École Normale Supérieure, the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and the Palace of Fontainebleau.

A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Adoniram Judson Eaton studied at Acadia, Harvard, Yale, and Leipzig (Ph.D.). He served as head of Amherst Academy and Woonsocket High School before becoming Associate Professor of Classics at McGill University in 1886.

Indologist Adriaan Scharpé studied at KU Leuven and Utrecht University, working under Albert Joseph Carnoy and Jan Gonda. He founded the Corpus Topographicum Indiae Antiquae and held long-term posts at Ghent University (1944–1979) and the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978).

Adrian Zenz, a scholar in Tibetology and sinology, completed his Ph.D. under Hildegard Diemberger at the University of Cambridge. He held teaching posts at the European School of Culture and Theology and became a Senior Fellow at the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation in 2019.

A scholar in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Adrien Barthélemy studied at INALCO and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under James Darmesteter. From 1909 to 1929, he taught at INALCO and was a directeur d’études at the EPHE.

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Adrienne Audrey G. Bennett served as librarian for the Buddhist Society (1949–1952), editor of The Middle Way (1951–1952), and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society (1956–1966).

Adrián Muñoz is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. His appointments include Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and lecturer of South Asian Religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Afeef Ahmed held a position at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar and studied as a Ph.D. candidate in South Asian Studies at Harvard University.

A scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Agata Bareja-Starzyńska conducted research at the universities of Oslo and Bonn. She has long been affiliated with the University of Warsaw as a Mongolist and Tibetologist.

Agathe Keller is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist who completed her PhD and Habilitation at Paris Diderot University. She has held research posts with the CNRS, REHSEIS, Paris Diderot University, and the University of Paris.

A scholar in Indology and religious studies, Agehananda Bharati studied under Erich Frauwallner in Vienna and at Sannyasi Mahavidyalaya. He taught across India, Thailand, and Japan before holding long-term posts at the University of Washington and Syracuse University.
Linguist and Indologist Agnes Margrethe Agerschou earned her M.A. from the University of Copenhagen by 1940. She worked as an assistant on the Critical Pāli Dictionary from 1940 to 1949.

Specializing in Tibetology and history/archaeology, Agnieszka Helman-Ważny studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University. She held posts at Cornell University, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Warsaw.
